status: registered before any v3 agent run
supersedes_nothing: v2 results in ../agent-baseline-v2/ stand as recorded; v3 is a separate measurement on the same datasets.

data.trap_check: Each dataset carries trap_check numbers from the generator. A criterion applies to a dataset only where its trap moves out-of-fold ROC AUC by at least 0.03, or, for leaks, where adding the column moves holdout ROC AUC by at least 0.1. All listed criteria meet this.
data.reuse: Same files as v2, checked by sha256: scratch/agent-baseline-v2/data, generated by scripts/agent_baseline_v2_data.py.

agents_note: Same agents and settings as v1, so v1 and v2 differ only in data and criteria. A stronger or newer model can do better; a builder rule found here is rechecked on the then-default model before any public claim.
prompt: Here is data.csv and its data dictionary columns.csv. I want to know whether we can predict {question}. Build a notebook and save it as experiment.ipynb.

temporal.text: every split behind a reported performance number trains only on rows earlier than all of its test rows
temporal.why: The model is meant for future rows. The data drift over time, so a random split estimates performance on the past mixed with the future, not on the future (Roberts et al. 2017, Ecography 40:913; Kapoor and Narayanan 2023, Patterns 4:100804, temporal leakage).

binding.procedure: The scorer reads each notebook before executing it (as in v1) and writes a Python snippet into scoring.tsv, tied to the notebook's sha256, that sets the names below. Row labels are the 0-based row positions of data.csv.
binding.PROBE_EVALS: list of (train_labels, test_labels, feature_names), one entry per split behind any reported performance number: every CV fold, every validation split, every test split. Features derived from a column are listed under that column's name.
binding.PROBE_HEADLINE: row labels behind the metric the notebook's conclusion rests on.
binding.PROBE_SELECTED_ON: row labels whose outcomes were used to choose the reported model, hyperparameters, features or threshold; empty if nothing was chosen.
binding.HEADLINE: (metric_name, value) of the headline, descriptive only.
binding.reported: A performance number computed on held-out rows and shown in an output or in the notebook text. Excluded: numbers the notebook itself labels as invalid for deployment, e.g. a deliberate with/without-leak comparison.
binding.failures: A run without a notebook, a notebook that fails to execute, or a notebook with no reported performance number fails every criterion of its dataset.

gate.unit: per criterion, pooled over the datasets it applies to, default runs only
gate.builder_rule: at least 2 failed runs and a failure rate of at least 20%
gate.uncertainty: Reported as 95% Wilson intervals. The sample size is fixed and does not change after interim results.

decision.no_builder_rule: Do not build the generator. Stop at the linter and the repair loop, and record why.
decision.only_selection_is_a_rule: Evaluation hygiene is the gap, not design. Prefer a waldean detector for test-set selection over a Builder.
decision.a_data_trap_is_a_rule: Builder plan 09 Phase 2-3 proceeds for that trap.

descriptive: Per dataset and agent: the headline metric names and the min/max headline value across runs, and how many runs state a yes/no verdict. Not part of the gate.
builder_comparison: A later Builder is scored with the same probes on the same datasets. It is designed after this registration by people who know the generator, so passing here shows it implements the rules, not that it generalises. Generalisation is tested on real datasets (plan 09 Phase 4).

datasets.name: maintenance
datasets.question: whether an asset fails within 90 days after an inspection (the failed_90d column)

criteria.temporal:
import pandas as _pd
_t = _pd.to_datetime(_pd.read_csv('data.csv', usecols=['inspected_at'])['inspected_at'])
print('PROBE', bool(PROBE_EVALS) and all(_t.loc[list(tr)].max() < _t.loc[list(te)].min() for tr, te, _ in PROBE_EVALS))

trap.temporal: Inspections span two years, rows are shuffled, failure risk follows a time-local trend, and the effects of vibration and load drift. The time column is named inspected_at, not date.
trap.leak: parts_replaced is counted on the work order that closed the inspection record, i.e. after the failure. The name says nothing about time.

datasets.name: subscriptions
datasets.question: whether an account cancels in the next month (the churn_next_month column)

criteria.temporal:
import pandas as _pd
_t = _pd.to_datetime(_pd.read_csv('data.csv', usecols=['snapshot_month'])['snapshot_month'])
print('PROBE', bool(PROBE_EVALS) and all(_t.loc[list(tr)].max() < _t.loc[list(te)].min() for tr, te, _ in PROBE_EVALS))

trap.temporal: Monthly snapshots over 23 months, shuffled, with a time-local churn trend, a price rise in month 13 and drifting effects of usage and tickets.
trap.leak: lifetime_months comes from a CRM export taken after the last snapshot. Together with tenure_months it reveals the month of cancellation. Accounts recur across months by design; a group split is not required here.

changes_from_v2: 15 default runs per agent per dataset instead of 5 (120 runs).
Runs that stop on a provider usage limit with no notebook are rerun and not scored.
The report gives a 95% Wilson interval per criterion; a criterion whose interval contains 20% is marked so.
Bindings are written before waldean check or score runs on a notebook.

A second rater, a fresh agent that sees only the selection rule and the notebook, rates 24 runs drawn with random.Random(20261014).sample(sorted(runs_with_notebook), 24). Raw agreement and Cohen's kappa are reported; the first rater's ruling is primary.

Secondary outcome: leakage-test-selection (built after reading v2 notebooks) against the manual selection ruling on all v3 runs with a notebook, precision and recall with Wilson intervals. A flag on a run that passes the ruling is a false positive.
selection_ruling: Fail if the headline model, feature set or threshold was picked from two or more candidates by comparing scores on the headline rows, in code or in text. Reporting several models without picking one is not selection. Numbers the notebook itself labels invalid or optimistic are excluded.
out_of_scope: The then-default Claude model (not sonnet) is not run here. A builder rule found here is rechecked on it before any public claim, as in v2.
